{{nihongo|'''Achihayao Shrine'''|阿遅速雄神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}, {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}, {{ill|Tsurumi-ku, Osaka|ca|Tsurumi (Osaka)|ceb|Tsurumi Ku (subdistrito sa Hapon, Ōsaka-fu)|eo|Kvartalo Curumi (Osako)|es|Tsurumi-ku (Osaka)|fa|تسورومی، اوساکا|fi|Tsurumi-ku (Osaka)|fr|Tsurumi-ku (Osaka)|it|Tsurumi-ku (Osaka)|ja|鶴見区 (大阪市)|ko|쓰루미구 (오사카시)|pl|Tsurumi (Osaka)|sco|Tsurumi-ku, Osaka|th|เขตสึรูมิ (โอซากะ)|tr|Tsurumi, Osaka|ur|سورومی وارڈ، اوساکا|zh|鶴見區 (大阪市)|zh_yue|鶴見區 (大阪)|qid=Q490526|lt=Tsurumi Ward}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Yatsurugi Shrine, but {{ill|Namikawa Seisho|ja|並河誠所|qid=Q6563872}}, who identified shrines listed in the Engishiki, determined that this shrine corresponded to the Ajihayao Shrine mentioned therein and erected a “stone shrine-name marker of Ajihayao Shrine.” From that time on, it came to be known as Ajihayao Shrine. {{nihongo|'''Achihayao Shrine'''|阿遅速雄神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* The principal deity is {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|es|Ajisukitakahikone|fr|Ajisukitakahikone|hu|Adzsiszukitakahikone|it|Ajisukitakahikone|ja|アヂスキタカヒコネ|mni|ꯑꯖꯤꯁꯨꯀꯤꯇꯀꯍꯤꯀꯣꯅꯦ|ru|Адзи-суки-така-хико-нэ|simple|Ajisukitakahikone|zh|味耜高彥根神|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami}} (あぢすきたかひこね).
* Also enshrined is {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q14944|qid=Q14944|lt=Yatsurugi Ōkami}} (やつるぎだいじん).

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|es|Ajisukitakahikone|fr|Ajisukitakahikone|hu|Adzsiszukitakahikone|it|Ajisukitakahikone|ja|アヂスキタカヒコネ|mni|ꯑꯖꯤꯁꯨꯀꯤꯇꯀꯍꯤꯀꯣꯅꯦ|ru|Адзи-суки-така-хико-нэ|simple|Ajisukitakahikone|zh|味耜高彥根神|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami}} descended to {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}, opened up the land, and taught the people agriculture. He was worshipped as the guardian deity of this area.

The origin of the shrine is said to date to {{ill|668|Q30116|qid=Q30116}} (the 7th year of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|Q314802|qid=Q314802}}), during the {{ill|theft of Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q861812|qid=Q861812}}. When the monk Dōgyō of {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}} attempted to flee back to {{ill|Silla|ar|مملكة شلا|ast|Silla (Corea)|az|Şila krallığı|azb|شیلا|bar|Silla|be|Сіла (дзяржава)|bg|Сила (държава)|bs|Kraljevstvo Sila|ca|Silla (Corea)|cdo|Sĭng-lò̤|ckb|شیللا|cs|Silla|da|Silla (koreansk stat)|de|Silla|eo|Silla|es|Silla (Corea)|eu|Silla (Korea)|fa|پادشاهی شیلا|fi|Silla|fr|Silla (Corée)|gl|Reino de Silla|hi|सिल्ला|hr|Kraljevstvo Sila|hu|Silla (ókori királyság)|id|Silla|it|Silla (Corea)|ja|新羅|ka|სილა|kk|Силла|km|ស៊ីលឡា|ko|신라|ks|سِللا سَلطَنَت|ku|Keyaniya Sillayê|lt|Šila (Korėja)|lv|Silla|mk|Сила (држава)|ml|സില്ല|mn|Шилла|ms|Silla|my|ရှီလာ|mzn|سیلا|nds|Silla|nl|Silla (Korea)|no|Silla|oc|Silla (reialme)|pl|Silla|pt|Silla (Coreia)|ro|Silla|ru|Силла|sco|Silla|sh|Sila (kraljevina)|si|සිල්ලා|simple|Silla|sk|Silla|sr|Сила (краљевство)|sv|Silla|sw|Silla|th|ชิลลา|tl|Silla|tr|Silla|uk|Сілла|vi|Tân La|wuu|新罗|zh|新罗|zh_classical|新羅|zh_min_nan|Sin-lô|zh_yue|新羅|qid=Q28456}} by boat with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusanagi Sword}}, he was caught in a sudden {{ill|Storm|Q81054|qid=Q81054}}. Fearing divine punishment, he threw the sword into a river mouth along the way. The sword was later recovered by local villagers and temporarily enshrined at this shrine. It is said that the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusanagi Sword}} was subsequently safely returned to {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065}}.

During the Meiji period, the shrine was relocated to its present site due to the construction of the {{ill|Naniwa Railway|Q11558476|qid=Q11558476}} (now the {{ill|Katamachi Line|Q1073379|qid=Q1073379}}).

In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 34 ({{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}), at the initiative of representatives of the {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}}, a {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Q1534477|qid=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku Shrine}} was built. At the same time, major improvements were made to the shrine grounds, including repairs to the main hall, expansion of the sacred precincts, and construction of subsidiary shrines. On the grounds remains a “Kikōhi” commemorative monument inscribed by {{ill|Governor of Osaka Prefecture|Q15063280|qid=Q15063280}} {{ill|Gisen Satō|Q11479713|qid=Q11479713}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑">According to the inscription on the Kikōhi monument in the shrine grounds</ref>

Even today, on the day of the {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}, the chief priest or shrine staff from {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065}} pay a visit, and on the festival day of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065}}, the priests of this shrine attend there, a custom that continues.

== Shrine grounds ==
[[File:Kinshi reishikeidaikinban.jpg|thumb|140px|left|The [[golden kite–shaped large brocade banner|Kinshi Reishikei Daikinban]] displayed only on special occasions, based on a myth that forms the origin of {{ill|Hanaten|Q11498911|qid=Q11498911}}]]
;Shrine buildings
:The main hall is built in the nagare-zukuri style with copper roofing.
;Shrine office
;Main gate
:Tiled roof. It is also called the Satsuma Gate, based on a tale that it was relocated from a nearby Satsuma residence in the early Meiji period.
;Stone shrine-name marker of Ajihayao Shrine
:A granite marker standing in front of the main hall. It is a square pillar 96 cm high and 24 cm on each side, engraved with “Ajihayao Shrine.” It was erected between {{ill|1736|Q6989|qid=Q6989}} and {{ill|1737|Q6993|qid=Q6993}} ({{ill|Genbun|Q1145754|qid=Q1145754}} 1–2) by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kubo Shigeyoshi}}, a disciple of Namikawa Seisho, who aimed to honor Shikinaisha in the Kinai region. The marker stands on a lower base stone 43 cm high and 61 cm square, and a middle base stone 24 cm high and 42 cm square. The middle base bears the name “Sugahirofusa,” referring to Yamaguchiya Iheei, who funded its construction. In {{ill|2004|Q2014|qid=Q2014}}, it was designated a {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|Q2901860|qid=Q2901860}} of Osaka City. <ref> {{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kyoiku/page/0000117783.html |title=Osaka City Designated Cultural Properties (FY2010) – Okage Lantern, 1 item (Ajihayao Shrine) |publisher=Osaka City |accessdate=2014-02-15}}</ref>
;Okage Lantern
:A lantern made in {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} ({{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 4), standing beside the main gate. It was erected as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=bond of pilgrimage}} for the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okage pilgrimage}}. It is the only surviving Okage lantern in Osaka City. In {{ill|2010|Q1995|qid=Q1995}}, it was designated an {{ill|Folk Cultural Property|Q24895900|qid=Q24895900|lt=Tangible Folk Cultural Property}} of {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}. <ref> {{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kyoiku/page/0000012464.html |title=Osaka City Designated Cultural Properties (FY2004) – Shrine-name markers of Amamizu Wake Toyoura-no-Mikoto Shrine, Kamisumuchi Shrine, Tame Shrine, and Ajihayao Shrine |publisher=Osaka City |accessdate=2014-02-15}}</ref>
;Great camphor tree
:A giant {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} said to be 1,000 years old, 16 meters tall with a trunk circumference of 6 meters. The main trunk died after being struck by {{ill|Lightning strike|Q15120872|qid=Q15120872}} in the Taishō period, but the subsidiary trunks remain healthy thanks to treatment by {{ill|tree doctors|Q24893891|qid=Q24893891}}. On February 20, {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 45), it was designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} by {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}} under the name “Camphor Tree of Ajihayao Shrine.” <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/bunkazaihogo/bunkazai/atihayaojinja_kusu.html |title=Osaka Prefecture Designated Natural Monument: Camphor Tree of Ajihayao Shrine |publisher=Osaka Prefecture |accessdate=2014-02-15}}</ref>
;{{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}}
:Two pairs (four statues) stand in front of the main hall. The pair at the rear was dedicated during the 1,300th anniversary festival held in {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 43). The pair at the front was dedicated in {{ill|1820|Q6973|qid=Q6973}} ({{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 3). <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/tsurumi/page/0000001385.html |title=The Great Camphor Tree of Ajihayao Shrine |publisher=Tsurumi Ward, Osaka City |accessdate=2014-02-15}}</ref>
;Guidepost
;Iris Sacred Pond
:Located on the north side of the shrine grounds. According to tradition, when {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}} fell ill, Ajisukitakahikone-no-Kami appeared in a dream and said, “If you offer the {{ill|Acorus calamus|Q158008|qid=Q158008|lt=shōbu}} from the pond east of the imperial palace, you will recover.” When this was done, the emperor was healed. During the summer festival, irises from this pond are cut, offered before the deities, and then distributed to parishioners. <ref name="菖蒲暦">{{Cite book |Japanese |year=2014 |title=Shōbu-goyomi |publisher=Ajihayao Shrine }}</ref> The pond was renovated in July {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑" />
;Auxiliary shrine
:Standing beside the main hall, enshrining {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi Ōkami}}, {{ill|Toshigami|Q3028663|qid=Q3028663|lt=Ōtoshi Ōkami}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi Ōkami}}, {{ill|Landlord deity|Q4160872|qid=Q4160872|lt=Ōjinushi Ōkami}}, {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Ōkami}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami}}, {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman Ōkami}}, and {{ill|Kotohira shrines|Q11646488|qid=Q11646488|lt=Kotohira Ōkami}}. <ref>Based on the inscription on the auxiliary shrine plaque</ref> Built in July {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑" />
;Taishōgun Shrine
:A subsidiary shrine enshrining the {{ill|Daishōgun (directional deity)|Q167008|qid=Q167008|lt=Taishōgun}}. Built in July {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑" />
;Camphor Tree Inari Shrine
:Built in July {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑" />
;Gokoku Shrine
:A subsidiary shrine enshrining those who died for the state. Built in July {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}}. <ref name="境内紀功碑" />

== Major festivals ==
* Summer Festival Eve – third Saturday of July
* Summer Festival – third Sunday of July
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Grand Annual Festival}} – third Saturday and Sunday of October

<ref name="菖蒲暦" />
== Access ==
200 meters east from {{ill|Hanaten Station|Q762983|qid=Q762983}} on the JR {{ill|Katamachi Line|Q1073379|qid=Q1073379|lt=Gakken Toshi Line}} and JR {{ill|Osaka Higashi Line|Q1067370|qid=Q1067370}}. Faces {{ill|Osaka Prefectural Road Route 159|Q11441277|qid=Q11441277}}.
